II. To bring his familiefamily to yethe Church or Congregation on the Sabbath day, to lookelook that they do religiously there behauebehave themseluesthemselves, & after the publikepublic exercises ended, & the Congregation is dismissed, to take account of that which they hauehave heard, that they may profit in knowledge and obedience. Act. 10. 24. The day after, they entredentered into Caesarea; Now Cornelius waited for them, & had called together his kinsmen & special friends. vers. 33. Now therefore (saith Cornelius to Peter) are we all heerehere present before God, to hearehear all things that are commanded thee of God. IobJob 1. 5. And when the daiesdays of their
banqueting were gone about, IobJob sent and sanctified them, & rose vpup early in the morning, & offredoffered burnt offerings, &c. 2. King. 4. 23. And he said, wherefore wilt thou go to him to day? It is neither new moonemoon nor Sabbath. For this very cause the fourth CōmandementCommandementCommandment is giuengiven first of all & principally to the master of the familiefamily, that he might see the Sabbath kept, and be a principal doer in all parts of Gods worship therein. Exod. 20. 10. In it thou shalt not do any workework, thou nor thy son, nor thy daughter, thy man-seruantservant, nor thy maid, nor thy cattelcattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates.

Neither is this his care tied only to the Sabbath, but vponupon other daiesdays besides it, he ought to cause them of his housholdhousehold, as much as in him lieth, to repairerepair to places, where the word of God is preached. Commendable was the practise of MarieMary the sister of Martha, in this case, who when Christ came to her house is said, to sit at his feetefeet and attend vntounto his preaching, Luk 10. 39.

III. To prouideprovide for his family meat, drinkedrink and clothing, and that they may
liuelive a quiet & peaceable life, 1. Tim. 5. 8. Pro. 27. 26. The lambs are for thy clothing, and the goats for the price of thy field. v. 27.

And let the milkemilk of thy goats be sufficient for thy food, for the food of thy familiefamily, and for the sustenance of thy maids. 1. Cor. 9. 9. Thou shalt not muzzle the mouth of the oxeox, that treadeth out the cornecorn: doth God care for oxen? eitherEither saith he it not altogether for our sakes? Matth. 13. 52. IV. To keepekeep order, and to exercise discipline in his house, and that in this manner:

In case of offence, when a capitallcapital crime is committed, which incurrethincureth publikepublic censure; he is not to punish it himselfehimself, but to bring the offender to the ciuillcivil Magistrate, to informeinform of his fault, that he may hauehave his desert: It was a course established by the IudicialJudicial law, which God gauegave vntounto Moses for his direction in causes criminallcriminal among the Israelites: Deut. 21. 18. 19. 20. If any man
hath a son that is stubbornestubborn, & disobedient, which wilwill not hearken vntounto the voice of his father, nor the voice of his mother, and they hauehave chastened him; then shalshall his father and his mother take him, and bring him out, vntounto the Elders of his citiecity, and vntounto the gate of the place where he dwelleth, and shall say vntounto the Elders of his citiecity; This our son is stubbornestubborn, and disobedient, and he will not obey our admonition: heehe is a rioter, and a drunkard. V. To giuegive intertainmententertainment to those that are strangers, & not of the familiefamily, if they be Christians, and BelieuersBelievers; but specially to the Ministers of the Word. Rom. 12. 13. GiuingGiving your seluesselves to hospitalitiehospitality. Hebr. 13. 2. div.head: CHAP. 18.
Of the MistresseMistress of the familieFamilyfamily, or Goodwife of the houseHouse.

For he is, as it were, the prince and chiecechief ruler; she is the associate, not only in office and authoritieauthority, but also in aduiseadvise, and counsellcounsel vntounto him. 1. King. 17. 17. The second dutieduty is, to giuegive the portion of food vntounto her familiefamily, or cause it to be giuengiven in due season. ProuProv. 31. 15. She riseth whiles it is yet night, and giuethgiveth

Quest. Whether may the goodwife, without the consent of the goodman, giuegive and bestow the goods belonging to the familiefamily?

The goods which are common to them both, are of another nature; and these sheeshe may not bestow, without his allowance, either expresseexpress or at least general and impliciteimplicit, specially when the giuinggiving of them doth or may grow in likelihood, to the hinderancehindrance, and preiudiceprejudice of the state of the familiefamily.
